blocking_findings.title: R3 calls the replacement completion authority existing and exact without naming or qualifying its binding and failure contract.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Split R3 into the ready explicit-state adapter removal and a gated completion cut. Name the existing attempt owner and artifact owner. Specify the material source/product identity, including event/document identity, source hash, extractor/prompt/model and relevant anchor inputs. Define output integrity and repair checks and the commit order across artifact, cache projection and attempt completion. If llm_artifact_store is the owner, require successful durable persistence and verified output before marking completion; its current best-effort (None, False) path must remain pending/failed. Do not add a new store. Prove changed-source, changed-anchor, missing/corrupt-output and write-failure recovery before deleting processed-state procedures.

required_changes: Revise R3 as stated above. Existing generic attempt fingerprints and best-effort artifact storage are reusable building blocks, not proof that an exact narrative-product completion contract already exists.

Keep R5's unresolved capture/disposition decision as a hard pre-cutover gate. Do not count native publication or a compatibility projection as a completed retirement until the producer no longer runs its independent legacy selection/publication sequence.
At implementation acceptance, enforce the proposal's own old-procedure deletion and caller migration requirements. Wrapper extraction or unused-helper deletion alone must not close any unit.
optional_changes: Put the original-source extraction feasibility decision early in Wave 2, even if implementation remains Wave 3. R4 is a larger reduction in information transformations than R6 or the first R3 adapter cut.

Add a small terminal lane map for the supported producer/document classes: active acquisition owner, processing owner, publication owner, read owner and remaining compatibility projection. This would make cumulative simplification easier to judge without invented deletion percentages.

Use one representative pre-earnings, post-earnings, progressive research/Q&A and portfolio-threshold journey as final cross-unit acceptance. Unit-level equality alone does not demonstrate the proposed one-evidence-flow endpoint.
unverified_claims: No current implementation, model-call savings, latency reduction, or whole-platform deletion percentage was verified or inferred.
The retained reader-cost artifacts contain the stated 1660/105 and 649/40 baseline counters, but this review did not rerun their instrumentation or independently validate runtime representativeness.
Original-document automated parity across transcripts, releases, investor updates and supplements remains unproved, as the proposal states.
R5 lossless unknown/rejected capture ownership, source-context completeness, transaction/replay/supersession parity remain open.
The existing full-suite teardown failure, current scheduler/runtime use, and physical legacy retirement qualification were not tested.
NU/MELI analytical-depth acceptance and source-byte reconciliation were not independently rerun.

unit_assessments.R1: Proceed first. Cohesive, bounded, no migration required. Audit extractor commits before claiming document atomicity; per-document recovery is the honest initial boundary.
unit_assessments.R2: Sound next-stage target. Preserve URL-presence skip, automatic/manual authorization, calendar forwarding and caller metadata effects. Classification before exact managed inventory is a real missing seam.
unit_assessments.R3: Revise before completion-state implementation. Adapter removal is independently useful but must not be represented as completion-authority retirement.
unit_assessments.R4: High ambition and direct product value. Class-by-class migration is realistic. Preserve original-context novelty, history, unknown/partial states and narrative generation.
unit_assessments.R5: High-value data-representation reduction, correctly blocked pending semantic/capture and recovery qualification. Do not force it into Wave 1 or physically delete history.
unit_assessments.R6: Real performance and ownership target, with existing batch machinery. Preserve clock semantics and local failure isolation; recursive derivation verification can limit gains.
unit_assessments.R7: Appropriate backend/render boundary change, not just navigation. workspace_data.py:193-213 and439-465 confirm anchor/filter/cache and Markdown parsing responsibilities. Preserve analytical selection as a prepared operation, then remove its render-time route.

judgments.sequence_assessment: R1 then R6 as separate changes is realistic and allows useful subtraction without native-table migration. Wave 2 can qualify managed registration and typed sections while the R3 completion contract is settled. R4/R5 per-class/per-producer gates avoid a speculative whole-platform cutover. The roadmap is ambitious enough to act on after the narrow R3 revision; its strongest claims are proposed cuts, not completed simplification. All seven units require actual active-call-path removal, and physical history retirement remains a separate authority.

judgments.confidence: High for the static architecture assessment; moderate for ultimate product improvement. Scores are advisory judgments, not measurements. No tests, live state, provider calls or network calls were used. The proposal and inventory hashes match the manifest. Application and test files are unchanged in the inspected worktree.
strongest_supported_cuts: R1 is immediately credible. Both 11-entry dispatch maps and both NU overrides exist. Quarterly _safe_extract converts input failures to zero (src/pipeline/quarterly_refresh.py:184-195), while its caller reports failure only for negative counts (:340-350). The CLI has a distinct failure path (execution/extract_facts.py:147-195). Combining the engines removes an active duplicate and corrects a false-success policy without requiring a database migration. The proposal correctly preserves refresh_cache's commit=False path (execution/refresh_cache.py:1183-1205).

R6 has a demonstrated repeated-work target. Discovery calls as_known and then fetches the selected bundle again per row (src/sources/discovery_financials.py:223-238). Report admission does the same (src/sources/report_financials.py:220-226). The retained .tmp/reader-reuse-comparison.json supports the stated 1660/105 and 649/40 baselines; its baseline and candidate sources are equal, so it proves cost only. The roadmap makes this distinction correctly. Existing batch provenance reads already return typed per-observation outcomes (src/provenance/fact_read_model.py:513-573).

R2 removes competing registration procedures rather than merely sharing a downloader. Its identified capability gap is real: automatic publication must preserve requested=False, whereas current managed preparation uses requested=True (execution/fetch_ir_documents.py:594; src/pipeline/managed_ir_sources.py:552). Bounded type/period triage and preserving the upload route are sensible qualification conditions.

R3's first cut is strong and independent of the harder completion cut. The state adapter mutates processor and index paths and rewrites sys.argv (execution/process_ir_documents_state.py:48-90). Explicit state arguments can retire this entire adapter while preserving process isolation where needed.

R4 is the most valuable semantic simplification. It removes a lossy generated-summary-to-number hop while retaining narrative analysis. The stated current limits are accurate: the original automated path defaults to ir_supplement and slices input before enumeration (src/compute/kpi_extract_summaries.py:1380,1557-1603); the caps are 200 and 80000 (:1069-1070). Class-by-class parity is a practical condition, and the proposal correctly avoids claiming fewer total model calls.

R5 correctly treats raw capture and semantic admission as different responsibilities. FactCellV2 requires reporting identity, period coordinates, basis and scope (src/provenance/fact_plane_v2.py:309-339); its basis/scope enums have no unknown value (:46-61). A native observation field is therefore not proof that an unclassified spreadsheet cell can replace its legacy capture. The explicit unresolved gate prevents an unsafe cutover. Current parsing does discard cell identity and raw representation (src/ir_pipeline/spreadsheet.py:120-164), and current ingestion commits periods independently (src/ir_pipeline/ingest.py:189-274).

R7 cuts a real architectural round trip and render-time dependency. workspace_data documents and implements Markdown parsing, LLM selection and its separate cache (src/report/renderers/workspace_data.py:1-16,160-274,439-469). workspace_html loads panels during rendering (:337-351) and a further database-backed value (:621). Existing section models are a suitable destination; retaining qualified analytical selection avoids accidentally reducing research depth.

blocking_findings.title: R3 assumes an exact narrative-completion receipt contract that the inspected existing owners do not yet provide
blocking_findings.evidence: Proposal lines 85-86 say JSON/cache success will be replaced with existing exact source/product attempt and artifact receipts. The narrative processor currently treats cache existence as completion and writes the file before marking the index (execution/process_ir_documents.py:166-197). run_accounting supplies logical invocation fingerprints and attempts, but material inputs must be supplied by its caller (src/pipeline/run_accounting.py:75-92); it does not by itself bind a narrative output file to completion. The obvious reusable artifact owner explicitly describes writes as best-effort when the database/table is missing (src/llm_artifact_store.py:15-16), and source_doc_ids are descriptive provenance excluded from the cache key (:88-91). These are useful owners, but their existence is not the exact fail-closed product-completion contract claimed here. No ready narrative-specific receipt owner is identified in the proposal or inventory. R5 names a comparable capability gap explicitly; R3 should do the same.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Keep the explicit-state adapter retirement independently ready. For the later JSON/cache retirement, name the existing attempt/artifact owners to extend and add a bounded qualification gate: the logical product key must cover immutable source versions plus material prompt/model/owner-context inputs; verified output identity must be bound to durable completion; a file-write/receipt-write interruption must reconcile without falsely completing work or billing an unchanged completed product again. State that this contract is to be qualified, rather than already present. No new store or generic workflow engine is needed.

required_changes: Resolve the R3 completion-contract finding in the roadmap before treating all seven units as implementation-ready. It does not block the independently scoped R1/R6 work or R3's explicit-state first cut.

Before each R1 implementation is accepted, inventory the commit closure of every selected extractor and receipt writer, not only its top-level function. Exercise a document with one valid record followed by malformed input. Verify rollback before failure accounting and preservation of earlier completed documents. This is already required in spirit by proposal lines 49-52 and must remain a delivery gate.

For R6, implement the report operation with separate resolution O and source/admission K cutoffs. read_as_known currently passes the observed cutoff to required_provenance_bundles (src/provenance/canonical_fact_resolution.py:525-532). The report contract instead reads sources at K (src/sources/report_financials.py:363-368). A direct call to the current required batch is insufficient for explicit O>K and for per-cell corruption isolation. Preserve the proposal's explicit-clock and distinct-failure tests.

Keep R4 and R5 qualification producer/class-local. R4 must enumerate the retained configured and novel population, original anchors, exclusions and partial/missing states before removing that class. R5 must identify a real lossless unadmitted/rejected capture owner and establish transaction/replay/recovery behavior before switching new writes. These are present design gates, not reasons to hold the earlier structural cuts.

Before claiming drastic platform simplification, show one end-to-end core task using the new flow and record actual active procedure/authority reductions, retained compatibility routes, reader cost and narrative coverage. The current seven MVPs prove local improvement; they do not yet prove the overall product claim. This can be a small acceptance table, not another framework or audit program.
optional_changes: Make the first source-class/producer selection for R4/R5 explicit after the initial structural cuts. Choose retained originals and adequate source context, so effort goes to a complete vertical slice rather than the hardest issuer first.

Use a compact before/after owner-and-call-path table as the cumulative subtraction record. Count active orchestration and authority paths, not only deleted lines or files. The proposal already requests per-change subtraction; the cumulative table will show whether compatibility paths are actually closing.

Do not let feature pruning wait for physical legacy retirement. The proposal correctly separates those actions. The two quarterly and one annual observation windows are current canonical policy (directives/data_provenance.md:616-629), not a technical prerequisite for R1, R2, R3's adapter, R6 or R7.
Keep R7 limited to one prepared section first. Moving all workspace panels at once would increase scope and could hide a regression in research depth without improving the proof.
unverified_claims: No candidate implementation, speedup, reduced production cost or seven-unit parity was verified. The proposal correctly states that none of the units is implemented.
The reader cost JSON and its instrumentation were inspected, not rerun. They describe synthetic fixtures and unchanged source. They do not establish production latency or future batching gains.
No full-suite result, teardown-failure diagnosis, live-use frequency, production reachability closure or scheduler migration was independently executed in this review.
NU/MELI research depth and byte reconciliation were not re-adjudicated. The proposal correctly keeps them separate from semantic/native acceptance.

No existing owner was proved sufficient for new unknown/unclassified/rejected spreadsheet capture. The legacy disposition capture seam retains legacy persisted fact rows (src/pipeline/kpi_legacy_disposition_capture.py:51-84); it is not by itself a demonstrated new spreadsheet capture path.
The review is independent advisory evidence. It grants no execution, collection, production, publication or deletion authority.

blocking_findings.title: The first performance milestone can pass without a material cost reduction.
blocking_findings.evidence: Proposal:166-176 records 1660/649 SELECTs and 105/40 verifier calls but requires only measurement and removal of direct redundant bundle fetches. It sets no accepted bound for the remaining total verification work, including recursive derivations. Proposal:205-217 records removed and added components but gives no net burden acceptance rule. Source already has bounded batching at src/provenance/canonical_fact_resolution.py:497-559 and src/provenance/fact_read_model.py:513-543, so moving callers alone does not prove that repeated verification inside the full operation is controlled. Replacing the in-memory hand schema at tests/test_pipeline_quarterly_refresh.py:32-178 with migrated_db improves schema fidelity, but lower setup time is unproven; tests/conftest.py:536-547 describes a cached migrated database, not a cost comparison.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Add one small Wave 1 scorecard to the roadmap. Bind the existing baseline populations to exact evidence artifacts. Require a stated bound on full-publication checks per distinct publication/cutoff/snapshot, counting recursive reads, zero direct consumer rereads, and a meaningful SELECT reduction. Record paired operation latency separately from test setup. For R1, require two active batch owners to become one and record deleted/new owning procedures plus cold/warm focused-test setup cost. Use explicit accepted regressions where integrity requires extra cost; do not require a platform-wide deletion percentage or create another benchmark framework.

blocking_findings.title: The product endpoint has no executable retained-task acceptance contract.
blocking_findings.evidence: Proposal:12-17 promises NU PRE/POST, MELI depth, owner context, scenarios, sensitivities and workbooks. The individual MVPs test documents, cells or one section; proposal:191-193 allows any one prepared section to satisfy R7. No bounded task matrix binds those cuts back to the promised research and portfolio outcomes. Proposal:236-237 correctly says artifact byte reconciliation is not semantic acceptance. The current derived report baseline is unavailable with ambiguous_table_coordinate at docs/quality/summary-kpi-completion-review.md:221-225, so preserving it alone cannot demonstrate a usable derived report value. src/report/renderers/workspace_html.py:348-351 still loads panel data during rendering; workspace_data.py:193-218 separately assembles owner/thesis context, filters with an LLM and caches the result. Moving that work must preserve the complete argument and invalidation semantics, not merely the displayed values.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: Name retained NU PRE, NU POST and MELI reference artifacts and define a compact acceptance matrix for a brief, deep research/Q&A, and a portfolio decision. State the expected source coverage, selected facts/citations, assumptions, thesis changes, scenarios/workbook formulas and degraded-state behavior for each affected path. Reuse existing fixtures and artifacts. Add a positive available derived-value case for R6, alongside unavailable/corrupt cases. Select a concrete R7 section with owner-context selection and prove its prepared typed result is reused across compact/full/evidence/export views, with zero DB/model work during its render and preserved invalidation/recovery. Schedule this acceptance with the relevant cuts, before feature pruning; no new provider calls or collection are authorized by writing the plan.
